overall_status: conditional mathematical advances and model-scope results; lead photon-rate theorem is internally composed from established phase-retrieval and quantum-estimation results; novelty, external proof review, polynomial-time recovery, and finite-precision instrument robustness unresolved

claims.statement: For d >= 2 and any complex sensing matrix A with m_+ nonzero rows, in the unnormalised ell_2 metric on squared intensities and quotient distance ||xx* - yy*||_*, beta_A^2 >= max{4, 2d(d+1)/m_+}.
assumptions: Peng-Han-Huang lower-constant variational formula applies
output coordinates are raw squared intensities with unnormalised ell_2 norm
claims.status: internally reconstructed deterministic bound; not a photon or detector-cost lower bound
claims.source_pointers: Peng-Han-Huang raw intensity map and lower-constant formula; Haar-random ordered orthonormal pair calculation is reconstructed in the linked report.
claims.novelty_boundary: The source paper's row-condition analysis is new; the m-dependent consequence here is elementary and not priority-cleared. It concerns deterministic additive ell_2 conditioning only.
claims.costs: Constant beta under this metric forces m_+=Omega(d^2). No statistical noise, photon count, channel precision, calibration, or detector background model is present.
claims.falsifier: A matrix within the stated interface violating the Haar upper bound L_A^2 <= S/[2d(d+1)] or the stated U_A lower bound.
claims.next_gate: Compare with likelihood-induced metrics under a fully charged physical count model; independent review of the Haar contraction.

claims.statement: For complex iid standard-Gaussian A in C^{m x d}, m >= C zeta^-2 log(1/zeta)d and fixed 0<zeta<0.05, with probability at least 1-6 exp(-c zeta^2 m), B=A(A*A)^(-1/2) is Parseval and its magnitude map satisfies || |Bx|-|By| ||_2 >= ell_zeta d_phi(x,y), ell_zeta=(1/beta_0-zeta)/sqrt(1+zeta), beta_0=sqrt(4/(4-pi)). Its rows define a complete m-outcome rank-one one-photon POVM.
assumptions: standard circular complex Gaussian row entries with E aa*=I
m satisfies the cited source sample-size condition
ideal exact whitening and calibrated frame
pure input state is normalized to unit norm
claims.status: conditional theorem; the random lower bound is source-reported and the Parseval whitening/POVM implication is internally derived
claims.source_pointers: Xia-Xu-Xu 2024, Lemma 4.2 and Theorem 4.3; B=A(A*A)^(-1/2), d_phi(S^(-1/2)x,S^(-1/2)y) >= d_phi(x,y)/sqrt(lambda_max(S)).
claims.novelty_boundary: The Gaussian magnitude stability and universal beta_0 are prior art. The exact one-photon Parseval-frame conversion is an internal synthesis and not priority-cleared.
claims.costs: m=O_zeta(d) channels for fixed zeta with hidden absolute constants; draw/store O(md) coefficients, preprocess O(md^2+d^3), and implement an m-output isometry. Finite-bit calibration and physical loss bounds are not established.
claims.falsifier: A flaw in the cited uniform magnitude stability theorem or a failure of the polar-normalization lower-modulus inequality on the stated good event.
claims.next_gate: Prove explicit finite-bit/calibration robustness for an implementable finite-precision Parseval frame and verify a physical compilation protocol.

claims.statement: For N fixed incident photons measured independently by the Parseval POVM above, the global minimum-Hellinger-distance estimator over unit pure states has uniform expected squared phase-quotient risk at most min{2, 4(m-1)/(N ell_zeta^2)}. Under independent Poisson photon flux tau, the full counts have Y_j~Pois(tau p_j(x)) and pairwise Bhattacharyya coefficient exp[-tau H^2(p_x,p_y)/2] <= exp[-tau ell_zeta^2 d_phi(x,y)^2/2].
assumptions: known calibrated Parseval POVM
unit pure state, identical independent input copies
all m outcomes are retained
ideal no-loss/no-dark-count model for the displayed bound
global minimizer of empirical Hellinger distance is returned
claims.status: internally proved conditional statistical guarantee; no efficient optimization guarantee
claims.source_pointers: Exact multinomial Hellinger expectation bound, triangle inequality, and product-Poisson affinity are derived in the linked report; prior Poisson phase-retrieval controls are listed there.
claims.novelty_boundary: Poisson likelihood, Hellinger geometry, and minimum-distance ideas are standard. Their composition with the whitened O(d)-outcome frame theorem is not priority-cleared. The report makes no algorithmic superiority claim over polynomial-time low-dose methods.
claims.costs: N incident photons exactly, or expected tau incident photons in the Poisson model. Risk is O(m/N) with fixed constants on the good-frame event. Uniform known efficiency eta costs a factor 1/eta; backgrounds and unknown gains are excluded. Exact global optimization is nonconvex; a gamma-net implementation is exponential in d.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to E H^2(p_hat,p) <= (m-1)/N, the MHD triangle bound, or the exact product-Poisson affinity formula.
claims.next_gate: Construct a polynomial-time estimator with the same uniform risk under low-dose counts; quantify dark-count, gain, and matrix-calibration perturbations.

claims.statement: For Haar-uniform unknown pure states in C^d, any procedure using N copies has expected squared phase-quotient error at least (d-1)/(N+d), because the optimal average fidelity is (N+1)/(N+d) and d_phi^2 >= 1-F pointwise. Hence the O(d/N) risk of the O(d)-outcome Parseval MHD procedure is minimax-rate optimal up to constants for N >= d.
assumptions: Haar prior over normalized pure states in C^d
N identical copies
arbitrary measurement and pure-state estimate permitted in the lower bound
squared quotient loss d_phi^2=2(1-|<x,y>|)
claims.status: established source theorem combined with an internally derived metric comparison
claims.novelty_boundary: The optimal fidelity result is established prior art. The claimed match is only in dimension/sample scaling, not in constants or minimax fidelity.
claims.costs: Counts every one of the N input copies and allows the lower-bound comparator arbitrary collective measurements; the upper instrument is a separable single-copy measurement.
claims.falsifier: A failure of the source fidelity theorem under the Haar prior, or an error in d_phi^2 >= 1-F.
claims.next_gate: Specialist review of the risk translation and compare finite-dimensional constants against known covariant POVM estimators.

claims.statement: The d^2 channel lower bound for beta=2 in unnormalised squared-intensity ell_2 does not imply a d^2 physical detector or photon lower bound for phase retrieval: the normalized random Parseval POVM has O(d) outcomes, uniform amplitude/Hellinger separation, and O(d/N) pure-state estimation risk.
assumptions: same known pure-state parameter family and calibrated frame
measurement error is multinomial or Poisson shot noise, not adversarial unweighted additive intensity error
ideal instrument or stated uniform known loss
claims.status: proved within the declared mathematical model; no claim about arbitrary physical devices or nature
claims.source_pointers: Combines claim RAW-INTENSITY-ROW-COUNT, claim PARSEVAL-GAUSSIAN-POVM-MODULUS, claim PHOTON-COUNT-HELLINGER-RISK, and the Haar prior lower bound.
claims.novelty_boundary: This rejects a cross-metric inference, not the raw-intensity theorem. The construction is a literature-grounded synthesis; novelty/priority is unresolved.
claims.costs: O(d) channels and O(d/epsilon^2) incident photon copies for fixed stability tolerance; O(md) design representation and exponential finite-net fitting; calibration and finite-precision costs remain open.
claims.falsifier: A hidden mismatch between the physical POVM probabilities and the amplitude map or a shot-noise law outside the declared model.
claims.next_gate: Finite precision/calibration robustness, efficient reconstruction, and an experimental instrument-level comparison against raw-intensity estimators.

claims.statement: With exactly N launched copies, known state-independent efficiency eta, independent erasures, and a recorded no-click flag, every estimator has Haar-prior expected squared phase-quotient error at least (d-1)/(N eta+d). The Parseval-frame minimum-Hellinger estimator with the no-click category has risk at most 4m/(N eta ell_zeta^2), so for m=Theta(d), fixed stability, and N eta >= d, both bounds scale as d/(N eta).
assumptions: Haar-uniform normalized pure state in C^d
N independently launched identical copies
each copy independently detected with known state-independent efficiency eta
no-click flag is recorded and carries no state information
ideal known calibrated Parseval POVM for the upper bound
claims.status: internally derived lower-bound extension of the established Bruess-Macchiavello fidelity theorem; conditional upper bound from the Cycle-2 Hellinger estimator; no novelty claim
claims.source_pointers: Condition on K~Binomial(N,eta) detected copies; use F_opt(K)=(K+1)/(K+d), concavity of f(k)=(k+1)/(k+d), and d_phi^2>=1-F. The upper bound follows from the no-click categorical distribution and the same MDE proof as (3).
claims.novelty_boundary: The fidelity theorem, erasure argument, and Hellinger MDE construction use established ingredients; this loss-matched rate comparison is an internal composition, not priority-cleared.
claims.costs: Charges all N incident copies, including no-clicks; known uniform loss costs a factor 1/eta. Unknown/nonuniform loss, backgrounds, source energy, and calibration are excluded.
claims.falsifier: A violation of the conditional optimal-fidelity bound or concavity step, or a counterexample to the categorical MDE upper bound under the stated erasure interface.
claims.next_gate: Independently review the loss lower-bound conditioning and prove robust rates with measured nonuniform efficiency, unknown gains, and backgrounds.

claims.statement: For d>=2 and nonzero complex sensing rows a_j=t_j u_j with positive lower constant, beta=2 in the unnormalised ell2 metric on raw squared intensities iff the weights p_j=t_j^4/sum_k t_k^4 and directions Pi_j=u_j u_j* form a weighted complex projective 2-design: sum_j p_j Pi_j tensor Pi_j = 2 P_sym/[d(d+1)].
assumptions: complex dimension d>=2
nonzero rows and positive lower phase-retrieval constant
source raw-intensity ell2 interface and nuclear quotient metric
claims.status: internally reconstructed equality characterization from the 2026 source proof and standard design identities; specialist priority review unresolved
claims.source_pointers: Compress to every complex two-plane; equality in the source two-dimensional lower-bound chain forces the quartic maximum to equal its Haar mean on every plane, hence constant on the full sphere; polarization gives the tensor identity. The converse is the projective 2-design moment contraction.
claims.novelty_boundary: Projective 2-design inversion and tight-IC results are prior art; this exact beta iff statement is a short source-specific consequence and is not priority-cleared. The source theorem has a d=1 exception beta=1.
claims.costs: Exact beta=2 needs at least d^2 nonzero rows. In every d, Jasper-Mixon gives an exact design and hence sensing matrix with d^2+O(d^1.525) rows. This deterministic objective charges neither photons nor calibration.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the equality propagation through the source restriction inequalities, the quartic constancy argument, or the complex polarization step.
claims.next_gate: Independent phase-retrieval/frame-theory review and broader exact-source prior-art check.

claims.statement: With F=sum_j p_j Pi_j tensor Pi_j, F0=2P_sym/[d(d+1)], C_d=2(d+2)(d+3)/[d(d+1)], and rho=(beta/2)^2-1, the internally derived one-way bound is ||F-F0||_F^2 <= C_d rho max(1,rho). For m<d^2, rho additionally obeys rho >= (d^2-m)/[C_d m(d+1)^2]; there is no uniform reverse implication from relative moment closeness to beta closeness, as deleting a complete-MUB vector yields beta>=2sqrt(2).
assumptions: complex d>=2
raw unnormalised squared-intensity ell2 phase-retrieval condition number
positive row weights p_j proportional to fourth powers of row norms
claims.status: internally derived theorem candidate with finite sanity checks; proof and priority not independently validated
claims.source_pointers: Haar-average over complex two-planes bounds L_A; the resulting one-sided quartic bound and zero Haar mean control E g^2; a fourth Haar moment contraction controls ||F-F0||_F. Partial transpose yields a trace-one PSD rank-m approximation lower bound.
claims.novelty_boundary: Approximate-design moment metrics and Welch bounds are existing literature. The beta-to-weighted-moment link may be source-specific, but priority is unknown. Lower gaps are not known sharp.
claims.costs: Rows m and weights are counted. No photon likelihood, calibration cost, or algorithmic measurement-design runtime is included.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the two-plane L_A bound, the stated Haar fourth-moment contraction, or the trace-constrained rank approximation argument.
claims.next_gate: Independent algebraic proof review, compare equal-weight constants to current strengthened Welch bounds, and seek sharp examples at fixed (m,d).

claims.statement: A special Bodmann-Haas/Sidon weighted projective 2-design yields an exact beta=2 one-photon POVM with q^2+d outcomes in dimension d when q>=d is an odd prime; two distinct coordinate states have squared Hellinger distance 2/(q+1), so Poisson flux tau requires at least (q+1)/2 log(1/[4 alpha(1-alpha)]) photons for both testing errors <=alpha.
assumptions: d>=2 and odd prime q>=d
the explicit Sidon set and layer-symmetric design
ideal coherent isometry, exact normalization, ideal counters, no loss/background
claims.status: internally derived instrument and testing formulas; floating-point checks d=2..10; no hardware validation
claims.source_pointers: Character projectors sum to (q^2/d)I and coordinate projectors sum to I; square-root design weights therefore normalize to the identity after a common scalar. Coordinate outcome laws differ only on two basis outcomes; use exact Poisson affinity and TV testing lower bound.
claims.novelty_boundary: The Sidon design is published prior art; physical normalization and the coordinate-pair cost comparison are internal construction/audit, with novelty unresolved.
claims.costs: q^2+d output channels and a d-to-(q^2+d) isometry, with two finite-field QFT branches. QFT depth, loss, calibration, and detector costs are unspecified.
claims.falsifier: Failure of the POVM completeness identity, design normalization, coordinate outcome law, or exact affinity lower-bound calculation.
claims.next_gate: Independent circuit/isometry review and compare a physically compiled finite-precision device against Parseval random-frame likelihood performance.

finite_checks.scope: One deterministic d=4,m=24 complex Gaussian fixture; Parseval residual 3.272e-15, probability mass residual 2.887e-15, truncated product-Poisson affinity discrepancy 1.665e-16, empirical Hellinger risk 0.099963 versus expectation upper 0.287500.
not_evidence_for: the global estimator theorem in all dimensions

finite_checks.scope: Floating point verification for d=2..10 of POVM completeness, 2-design moment, exact inverse, and coordinate-state Hellinger distance; residuals are at machine precision.
not_evidence_for: all-d proof beyond the algebraic derivation
physical unitary synthesis or hardware loss

astra_boundary.scope_note: N66 requires a known product sensor/reference and a coordinate-specific post-storage query; N92 is scoped to supplied compatible channel classes; N93 leaves the general bounded-Holevo-to-EB implication open. None is a proof premise for the phase-retrieval count law.

summary: Hellinger/Poisson geometry yields an O(d)-outcome Parseval one-photon POVM with O(d/N) pure-state phase risk, matching Haar-average quantum lower-bound scaling; the d^2 exact-design row requirement belongs to a different raw squared-intensity ell2 criterion. Other branches are scoped model theorems and principled boundaries, not validated application discoveries.
